title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, tool schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Asha Patel
description: Implements OpenAI-compat function/tool calling refinements: 1) formalizes tool_choice semantics to match OpenAI behavior when multiple tool candidates are suggested by the model, including deterministic tie-breaking and a clear precedence rule for schema-exact matches; 2) adds schema mapping utilities so Redwood tool schemas can be auto-mapped to OpenAI-compatible JSON Schema snippets used for model-side validation and tool selection; 3) standardizes tool message formatting and streaming events so tool_call/tool_response events are emitted consistently for both streaming and non-streaming paths; and 4) updates SDK helpers and docs to reflect the compatibility layer changes. Motivation: customers using the OpenAI compatibility layer were seeing ambiguous tool selection when models returned multiple tool recommendations, and message formatting differences created downstream parsing bugs in some SDKs. This PR unifies behavior across hosted and private deployments and reduces edge-case differences between Redwood native tool-calling and OpenAI semantics. Changes include behavioral tests and doc examples. Checklist: - [x] Implement tool_choice precedence and tie-breaking - [x] Add schema mapping conversion helpers - [x] Normalize tool message envelope and streaming events - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Update docs and SDK helpers - [x] Run perf tests and CI

review_comments: Luis Gomez: Could you clarify tie-breaking order? If two tools both exactly match the schema, do we pick the first declared in the request or first returned by the model? Please add deterministic tests.

Asha Patel: We now prefer schema-exact matches first, then model order. If multiple exact matches exist we break ties deterministically by head_branch commit timestamp (consistent across runtimes). Added tests to test_tool_choice.py to cover both cases.

Priya Nair: Streaming path previously emitted a raw tool invocation string which SDKs parsed differently. Can we emit a canonical event with 'tool_call' and structured payload in both streaming and non-streaming flows?

Asha Patel: Yes, the streaming runtime now emits 'tool_call' events with a structured envelope and a 'tool_response' event when the tool finishes. The non-streaming path uses the same envelope. Added compatibility shims in openai_compat.py for older SDK callers.
Ethan Zhao: Minor: update docs with migration steps and example for multi-tool selection. Also note performance implications of schema validation on hot paths.

Asha Patel: Docs updated and added a note in Optimize recommendations to only enable schema mapping for high-confidence routes; perf tests show ~2% p99 increase in worst-case but average token cost improves due to fewer fallbacks.
Luis Gomez: CI flake in e2e-streaming on first run, reran and passed. Approved.
